doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

title: Cutting tape as a kid and loving group studio work
summary: His father bought a Webcor recorder, he learned to splice tape, and he preferred collaborative studio work to solitary cello practice.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That was my next question. The first time you took a razor blade to tape —

I was a kid. I remember being in my mom's house when I was little and my dad bought me a Webcor portable tape recorder. It was the first one that could sit like this on a desk. I mean it wasn't gigantic, it was just like this. And it had reel—to—reel. And I remember I played the cello and then I turned it around the other thing and I tried to play another cello part and it was delayed obviously. I couldn't figure that out yet because that was — those guys were moving the heads and they were figuring how to time delay multi—track recording and stuff. I didn't know that. But I would take a razor blade and I would cut. And I had editing tape. And I enjoyed it. I actually liked it. You know playing the cello was hard. And this was not as hard in a way but it was really enjoyable. And then playing the cello was a solitary thing. You went in a room and you practiced for hours and hours and hours to get good, by yourself. You went to visit your professor once a week, or you played chamber music once a week, orchestra twice a week. So what is that, a grand total of twelve hours? Making a film with a great writer and a great animator and a great voiceover narrator and all that stuff, it was a group of people in the booth. It was like playing quartets all the time. I mean I enjoyed the camaraderie. And I loved that about making rhythm & blues records too. You know not that I was like them because I wasn't like them. I was a cello player from Kensington with my own life. But did I enjoy my time spent with them? I loved it. You know and one of the things I have to say in the early '70s, I loved smoking reefer and they smoked reefer too so in a way my classical musicians no one smoked reefer in those days, very few people did. But the jazz musicians and the R&B musicians they did.
